Subject: Weekly MAP checkpoint — performance lab results & tuning plan

Hi Emma / SigmaHealth team,

Attaching the week-1 lab outputs ahead of our weekly MAP checkpoint next Wed (Aug 4). Key artifacts: latency_results_q2.csv (per-path p50/p95/p99), throughput_profile.pdf (sustained qps at different batch sizes), and MAP-v3.xlsx (mutual action plan updated).

Quick summary:
- Lab target: run your main inference scenario (seq len ~512, top-k sampling) at 100 concurrent sessions.
- p50 looks good (~48ms token), p95 ~240ms, p99 spikes at ~480ms in our baseline runs.
- Throughput plateaued at ~230 reqs/s with continuous batching; higher burst throughput requires smaller batching windows.

Open questions for the checkpoint:
1) Prioritization: do we optimize for p99 tail or steady-state throughput for your user flows?
2) Acceptable latency SLO at 95/99 for clinical triage UI (we documented two candidate SLOs in MAP-v3).
3) Finalize acceptance test (load profile + eval prompts) to sign-off.

Action requests before Wed:
- Emma: confirm which SLO (p95 or p99) to prioritize and share any additional evaluation prompts by Mon EOD.
- Marcus: run quantized-run at 4-bit profile and attach delta to the CSV by Tue.
- Karthik: schedule an extended load run for Tue night (simulate 10k tokens/session to capture KV cache effects).

Thanks — have included owners in CC. We can pivot the agenda based on Emma's SLO pick.

Cheers,

- For the clinical triage UI we need to target p95 <= 300ms and p99 <= 600ms. p95 is the main UX signal but p99 is a hard constraint for regulatory QA.

Folks — ran the 4-bit quantized profile last night and uploaded a short summary to throughput_profile.pdf (see section 3). Highlights:
- Quantized run reduced median token time by ~12% and p95 by ~18% in the 256 token path.
- p99 improvement varied; biggest wins only when KV cache hits were >85%.
- At full load (100 concurrent sessions), sustained throughput moved from 230 to ~265 reqs/s but tail variance persisted.

Proposed next tests (I can own these, need a slot):
A) KV warm-start test: pre-populate KV cache using synthetic warmup traffic, then run 2 hours of steady load. (Owner: Marcus; due Tue 08/04 morning)
B) Narrow-batch tuning: measure p99 while decreasing batch windows from 50ms -> 10ms across runs (Owner: Karthik; due Wed 08/05)
C) Eval run with SigmaHealth prompts (Owner: Marcus + Diego; need the prompt set from Emma by Mon EOD)

I've attached the partial CSV (latency_results_q2.csv) with markers for quantized vs baseline. Let me know if we should include extra kernel-level traces — they add ~10% overhead but clarify where the tail originates.

Hi all — thanks for the checkpoint this morning. Recap of what we agreed and owners/due dates (copying into MAP-v3):

Decisions made:
- Primary acceptance SLOs for go/no-go: p95 <= 300ms, p99 <= 600ms, cost <= $45 / 1k tokens.
- Emphasize KV warm-start strategy as primary mitigation for tail spikes; quantization is complementary.

Action items and owners (final):
- Marcus: complete KV warm-start test, attach full logs and updated latency_results_q2.csv (due 2026-08-04 09:00 PDT) — COMPLETED and uploaded.
- Karthik: run narrow-batch sweep and post results to Drive; add run IDs to MAP-v3 (due 2026-08-05 12:00 PDT).
- Diego + Marcus: run eval with SigmaHealth prompt set once Emma uploads prompts (target 2026-08-05 18:00 PDT).
- Emma: upload 30–40 prompt set and confirm any additional regulatory evals (due 2026-07-31 EOD — received).
- Marissa: coordinate prod ramp checklist including pre-prod cyber review and procurement sign-off (due 2026-08-07).

Notes / follow-ups:
- Marcus reported quantization reduced median and p95, but p99 improvement depends heavily on cache hit rate. We agreed to use the warm-start as the primary control.
- We will run a cost sensitivity once the eval run completes; Diego will pull projected token volumes and estimated unit costs into MAP-v3 under "Cost Scenarios."

Next checkpoint: Fri 2026-08-07 08:30 PDT (standup to confirm narrow-batch results and go/no-go recommendation).

If anyone needs to escalate earlier, reply-all and we'll pull in Alex / Sales.
